title: To Copy or Not to Copy: Copying Is Easier to Induce Than Recall
reasoning: The paper focuses on the mechanistic interpretability of LLMs, specifically how they arbitrate between parametric knowledge and contextual information, and how to steer their behavior (copying vs. recalling) using intervention vectors. It uses QA benchmarks and analyzes attention routing, MLP contributions, and probability trajectories. There is no component of evaluating or benchmarking religion, morals, or ethics as a core focus, nor is there a dedicated section on ethical considerations that goes beyond standard limitations.
